#
**API Agreement**

**Last Updated: March 26, 2026**

If you are agreeing to the Developer Terms on behalf of an entity, then you represent and warrant that you have authority to bind that entity, that you are doing so on behalf of that entity, and that all references to “you” in this agreement refer to that entity.

“Customer” means a business customer of the Services and includes any authorized users.

“Customer Data” means any data, including documentation, information, content or other material, that is transmitted by or accessible through the Ramp APIs, including any Personal Data contained therein.

“Developer Account” means an account with Ramp that is used to access Ramp APIs.

“Dispute” means any dispute, controversy, and claim resulting from a party’s rights and obligations under, or in connection with, the Developer Terms.

“Feedback” means all feedback, suggestions, ideas, or enhancement requests you submit or otherwise communicate by any means.

“Personal Data” means personal information or personal data, as defined under applicable data protection law.

“Ramp Account” means a Customer’s Ramp account used to access Services.

“Ramp APIs” means (i) any software, code, services, accounts, keys, or information related to Ramp’s application programming interface, including the developer console and all other tools, elements, components and executables, (ii) any Ramp-provided or Ramp-authorized protocol, server, connector, or interface that enables programmatic or automated access to Customer Data or Services, including any model context protocol (“MCP”) server, command line interface, agent tool interface, or similar technology, whether existing now or developed in the future, and (iii) documentation that Ramp makes available to help enable use.

“Services” means the finance automation and spend management services made available by Ramp to Customers.
